case: Eurodrone fictional eco-design and supply resilience

cues.text: Welcome to ASRI. This tutorial follows a complete eco-design and supply resilience case from start to finish.
Select Create Your Own Strategic Case. This journey is separate from the original maintenance demonstration.
Investigate presents four examples. We will use Eurodrone to examine critical materials and long-term support.
Select Eco-design and Critical Materials. The app loads a case and three fictional options.
The case concerns a hypothetical support subsystem. No figures here come from an actual Eurodrone programme.
The decision is whether qualified repair and supplier diversification might reduce long-term vulnerability.
Before comparing options, define the same component, functional requirements and assessment period.
We continue to Challenge, where operating and economic assumptions drive the comparison.
We compare the baseline, qualified repair, and repair combined with an additional qualified supplier.
All cases share the same six sections. What changes is which parameters apply to a particular decision.
Open Operational Conditions. Every input contains values for all three options, measured in matching units.
Recovery time describes how long each option would take without additional failures or disruptions.
The supply lead time captures a binding delay from a supplier or component, when that dependency applies.
The recovery deadline is shared. The model checks whether each strategy meets it under stated risk assumptions.
Open Risks and Probabilities. These values are practice assumptions, not calibrated forecasts.
We separate the probability of technical success from the delay incurred if the chosen route fails.
We also model the chance of an external disruption and the additional delay it could cause.
Economic Obligations covers direct cost, logistics and extra expenses under adverse conditions.
Expected cost weights conditional expenses by probability. It is not an approved contract price.
Contractual Conditions covers reservation fees and cancellation charges, only when they actually apply.
If a contract does not apply, mark Not Applicable and explain why. Do not invent a numeric zero.
Environmental Factors covers material demand, waste and greenhouse gases for a defined assessment boundary.
These quantities can be compared, but they are not a complete or certified life-cycle assessment.
The sixth section reminds us to trace and review inputs. An assumption does not become evidence on its own.
The results compare timelines, deadline performance, cost and environmental factors without declaring an automatic winner.
Let us change the repair option's recovery time and observe how the model responds.
The calculation updates as soon as an input changes. We can inspect sensitivity before making a decision.
We restore the original illustrative value so the remaining analysis uses a consistent baseline.
The sensitivity margin tests robustness. It is not a statistical confidence interval.
One option can improve a metric and worsen another. ASRI makes that trade-off visible.
Next comes Check. These calculations alone cannot establish a demonstrated benefit.
Check examines the quality of the inputs and the technical requirements that still need verification.
Four review gates cover comparable scope, technical eligibility, measurement methods and independent review.
We do not claim these gates have passed. This is a fictional example, and tick boxes do not replace approval.
The evidence register can identify a document, its owner, reviewer, review date and limitations.
We add a sample evidence record and leave it pending. This illustrates what a real case would still need.
Each baseline and option measurement would then need a traceable and comparable source.
Validation remains incomplete. That is intentional: a learning scenario must not be confused with actual performance.
With those limitations clear, continue to Translate for audience-specific communication.
Translate turns case findings into strategic arguments without changing the underlying numbers.
For a Defence customer, the focus is operational continuity and access to critical components.
For Engineering, the argument concerns qualification, safety and demonstrable repairability.
For a Programme Manager, the key issues are delivery commitments, cost and supply resilience over time.
For leadership, potential value is lower industrial dependency with transparent costs and uncertainties.
We can select the other alternative. The narrative should reflect the new comparison.
The report explicitly flags unvalidated data. A compelling narrative is not evidence of causality.
Finally, we review exports. We can generate a report and keep an editable copy of the case.
The PDF report includes assumptions, comparisons, pending evidence and qualified conclusions.
A Markdown version is also available for further review and editing.
Before sharing, check comparability and ensure no benefit is presented as validated without evidence.
To resume later, download a local case file. ASRI does not automatically store this work in the cloud.
That completes all four stages using Eurodrone. This is a hypothetical decision exercise, not a calibrated prediction.
